title: Canada immigration agency issues important clarification for international students 'who plan to work while studying' after work permits of Indian students were rejected
summary: Canada's immigration authority issued a clarification for international students after reports that some Indian applicants had work permits rejected. The agency reiterated how existing student work rules are applied and urged applicants to check documentation and eligibility requirements. Authorities encouraged students to consult official guidance and confirmed no broad policy change was announced.
content:
Reports emerged that several work-permit applications linked to Indian students were rejected, prompting a response from Canada's immigration agency. In a clarification note, the agency reiterated the framework governing international students who wish to work while enrolled in Canadian institutions. Officials emphasized that eligibility depends on the type of study permit held, the nature of the academic program, and compliance with documentation and application requirements.

The agency reminded students that off-campus work, co-op placements, and internships each have specific rules: off-campus employment is allowed under certain conditions tied to the study permit, while work integrated learning (such as co-op or internships) typically requires an explicit authorization or documented program requirement. The clarification aimed to address confusion and to encourage applicants to review eligibility criteria carefully before applying for work permits.

For students from India and other countries who experienced refusals, the agency advised reviewing the specific refusal letters, ensuring all requested documentation was provided, and, where appropriate, seeking guidance from designated learning institutions or accredited immigration advisors. The agency also urged applicants to use official online tools and checklists to confirm eligibility and to correct any application errors that can lead to refusals.

While the clarification did not signal a change in policy, it served to reassure international students that the core rules remain in place and that decisions are made on an application-by-application basis. The agency encouraged students to monitor official channels for updates and to allow sufficient processing time when preparing applications for study and work authorizations.

Students planning to work while studying are recommended to maintain clear records of their enrollment status, program requirements, and any employer agreements; to submit complete and accurate applications; and to contact immigration authorities or their institutions if they receive a refusal or face uncertainty. For authoritative guidance, applicants should consult the immigration agency's official website and materials provided by their educational institutions.

- The clarification aimed to address confusion and to encourage applicants to review eligibility criteria carefully before applying for work permits.

- Ensuring all requested documentation was provided.

The agency encouraged students to monitor official channels for updates and to allow sufficient processing time when preparing applications for study and work authorizations.

Students planning to work while studying are recommended to:
